e-5903.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Matrix
e-5903.problem: Find $B=\overline{A},$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/25ce0cd375da320d1615cf49f659ec33e4646cf6bc66455198bec5fd591b3dd3.png) What is the value of $b_{11} + b_{23}?$
e-5903.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} & 3-\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 3\text{i} & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} & 3+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 1-2\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & -3\text{i} & -2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b_{11} + b_{23} = (-4\textrm{i}) + (1-2\textrm{i}) = 1-6\textrm{i}.$

e-5525.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
e-5525.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/9e1718bbf8790a9cc89d7cc1c6dd7879f8e222f348e5a9a56fec83a1b033250d.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/e99949f7e98aee85a040f698b15822927d7aabea1e688337d209c8e1d08850d6.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/642f01152b6a1717300120241f788a24098413648cd70e8d0399629f11be2254.png) then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
e-5525.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & -5-7\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} & 5-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=2,d=5,e=-3$ and $h=-9.$ Therefore,

$$
ad+eh=2 \cdot 5 + (-3) \cdot (-9) = 37.
$$

e-5902.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 1 & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-\text{i})\cdot (1+2\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & (-\text{i})\cdot (1-\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot 2 \\ 1\cdot (1+2\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & 1\cdot (1-\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-\text{i})+(-1) & (-1-\text{i})+2\text{i} \\ (1+2\text{i})+(-2) & (1-\text{i})+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -1+\text{i} \\ -1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where $A=[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}?$
after.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{7-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{6+4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{7-4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4+9\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7+\text{i} & 6-4\text{i} \\ 7+4\text{i} & 4-9\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}=(6-4\text{i})-(7+4\text{i})=-1-8\text{i}.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where

after.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3-2\text{i} & 4\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i} & 5 & 3-5\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} & -5-\text{i} & -3+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4} & \overset{―}{3-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-1-3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{5} & \overset{―}{3-5\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2+\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-5-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-3+3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3+2\text{i} & -4\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i} & 5 & 3+5\text{i} \\ 2-\text{i} & -5+\text{i} & -3-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3-2\text{i} & 4\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i} & 5 & 3-5\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} & -5-\text{i} & -3+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{31}+{b}_{32}?$
content.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3-2\text{i} & 4\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i} & 5 & 3-5\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} & -5-\text{i} & -3+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4} & \overset{―}{3-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-1-3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{5} & \overset{―}{3-5\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2+\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-5-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-3+3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3+2\text{i} & -4\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i} & 5 & 3+5\text{i} \\ 2-\text{i} & -5+\text{i} & -3-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{31}+{b}_{32}=(2-\text{i})+(-5+\text{i})=-3.$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where $A=[\begin{aligned}9-7\text{i} & -2\text{i} & 6-\text{i} \\ -7 & 5-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 6 & -\text{i} & 0\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{21}+{b}_{32}?$
after.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}9-7\text{i} & -2\text{i} & 6-\text{i} \\ -7 & 5-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 6 & -\text{i} & 0\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{9-7\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{6-\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-7} & \overset{―}{5-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{6} & \overset{―}{-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{0}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9+7\text{i} & 2\text{i} & 6+\text{i} \\ -7 & 5+\text{i} & -\text{i} \\ 6 & \text{i} & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

decision.explanation: The imaginary part consists of the coefficients of i in each entry: −7, −4, 6, and 0. The real entry −5 has imaginary part 0.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Find the imaginary part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 6\text{i} & -5\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 6\text{i} & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 0+6\text{i} & -5+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Im}(A)=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
content.problem: Find the imaginary part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 6\text{i} & -5\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 6\text{i} & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 0+6\text{i} & -5+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Im}(A)=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}].$

after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} & 5\text{i} \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0-3\text{i} & 0+5\text{i} \\ -4+0\text{i} & 5+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}

$$
ah-cf=0\cdot 0-(-4)\cdot 5=20.
$$

after.html:
Question 8
?

If Re(x)=[abcd] and Im(x)=[efgh] are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix A=[2−3i1−i1+i5i] then what is the value of cd+gh?

a
7
b
5
c
10
d
15
e
6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For the given matrix A, we have that

A=[2−3i1−i1+i5i]=[2−3i1−i1+i0+5i]=[2110]⏟Re(A)+i[−3−115]⏟Im(A).

So we have c=1,d=0,g=1 and h=5. Therefore, cd+gh=1⋅0+1⋅5=5.

content.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
content.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}e & f \\ g & h\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} & 5\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $cd+gh?$
content.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} & 5\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} & 0+5\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $c=1,d=0,g=1$ and $h=5.$ Therefore,

$$
cd+gh=1\cdot 0+1\cdot 5=5.
$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: Find the real part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ 0-\text{i} & 4+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Re}(A)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
content.problem: Find the real part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 7-6\text{i} \\ 0-\text{i} & 4+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Re}(A)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}e & f \\ g & h\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 2-3\text{i} & 1-6\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
after.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 2-3\text{i} & 1-6\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}

$$
ad+eh=3\cdot 1+5\cdot (-6)=-27.

before.html:
Question 11
?

If A=[2−i3+i1+2i1+i] and B=[1+i2+i−2+i1−i], then AB=

a
[−4+2i9−2i−4+2i2+5i]
b
[5i+29−2i−4+2i−4+2i]
c
[−49−2i−4+2i7]
d
[−4−4+2i9−2i2+5i]
e
[5i+2−4+2i9−2i−4+2i]
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiplying rows of A by columns of B and using i²=−1 gives the entries −4+2i, 9−2i, −4+2i, and 2+5i, respectively. Thus AB matches option a.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 3+\text{i} \\ 1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 2+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-\text{i})(1+\text{i})+(3+\text{i})(-2+\text{i}) & (2-\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(3+\text{i})(1-\text{i}) \\ (1+2\text{i})(1+\text{i})+(1+\text{i})(-2+\text{i}) & (1+2\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(1+\text{i})(1-\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(3+\text{i})+(-7+\text{i}) & 5+(4-2\text{i}) \\ (-1+3\text{i})+(-3-\text{i}) & 2+5\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4+2\text{i} & 9-2\text{i} \\ -4+2\text{i} & 2+5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

If A=[2−i3+i1+2i1+i] and B=[1+i2+i−2+i1−i], then AB=

a
[−4+2i9−2i−4+2i2+5i]
b
[5i+29−2i−4+2i−4+2i]
c
[−49−2i−4+2i7]
d
[−4−4+2i9−2i2+5i]
e
[5i+2−4+2i9−2i−4+2i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

AB=[2−i3+i1+2i1+i]⋅[1+i2+i−2+i1−i]=[(2−i)(1+i)+(3+i)(−2+i)(2−i)(2+i)+(3+i)(1−i)(1+2i)(1+i)+(1+i)(−2+i)(1+2i)(2+i)+(1+i)(1−i)]=[(3+i)+(−7+i)5+(4−2i)(−1+3i)+(−3−i)2+5i]=[−4+2i9−2i−4+2i2+5i].

Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 3+\text{i} \\ 1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 2+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-\text{i})(1+\text{i})+(3+\text{i})(-2+\text{i}) & (2-\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(3+\text{i})(1-\text{i}) \\ (1+2\text{i})(1+\text{i})+(1+\text{i})(-2+\text{i}) & (1+2\text{i})(2+\text{i})+(1+\text{i})(1-\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(3+\text{i})+(-7+\text{i}) & 5+(4-2\text{i}) \\ (-1+3\text{i})+(-3-\text{i}) & 2+5\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4+2\text{i} & 9-2\text{i} \\ -4+2\text{i} & 2+5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 3 & -1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2\text{i} & 5 \\ 1-4\text{i} & 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-3\text{i})\cdot 2\text{i}+\text{i}\cdot (1-4\text{i}) & (2-3\text{i})\cdot 5+\text{i}\cdot (2+\text{i}) \\ 3\cdot 2\text{i}+(-1-\text{i})(1-4\text{i}) & 3\cdot 5+(-1-\text{i})(2+\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(4\text{i}+6)+(\text{i}+4) & (10-15\text{i})+(2\text{i}-1) \\ 6\text{i}+(-5+3\text{i}) & 15+(-1-3\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10+5\text{i} & 9-13\text{i} \\ -5+9\text{i} & 14-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

If A=[2−3ii3−1−i] and B=[2i51−4i2+i], then AB=

a
[14−3i9−13i−5+9i10+5i]
b
[10+5i9−13i−5+9i14−3i]
c
[−5+9i9−13i10+5i14−3i]
d
[−5+9i14−3i10+5i9−13i]
e
[10+5i14−3i−5+9i9−13i]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get AB=[2−3ii3−1−i]⋅[2i51−4i2+i]=[(2−3i)⋅2i+i⋅(1−4i)(2−3i)⋅5+i⋅(2+i)3⋅2i+(−1−i)(1−4i)3⋅5+(−1−i)(2+i)]=[(4i+6)+(i+4)(10−15i)+(2i−1)6i+(−5+3i)15+(−1−3i)]=[10+5i9−13i−5+9i14−3i].

verification.explanation: Rechecking the row-by-column products gives 10+5i, 9−13i, −5+9i, and 14−3i in their respective positions. This agrees with the worked solution and confirms option b.

content.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 3 & -1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2\text{i} & 5 \\ 1-4\text{i} & 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-3\text{i})\cdot 2\text{i}+\text{i}\cdot (1-4\text{i}) & (2-3\text{i})\cdot 5+\text{i}\cdot (2+\text{i}) \\ 3\cdot 2\text{i}+(-1-\text{i})(1-4\text{i}) & 3\cdot 5+(-1-\text{i})(2+\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(4\text{i}+6)+(\text{i}+4) & (10-15\text{i})+(2\text{i}-1) \\ 6\text{i}+(-5+3\text{i}) & 15+(-1-3\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10+5\text{i} & 9-13\text{i} \\ -5+9\text{i} & 14-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}3+\text{i} & -\text{i} & 1-4\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i} & 1+\text{i} & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i} \\ 1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(3+\text{i})(1+\text{i})+(-\text{i})(1-\text{i})+(1-4\text{i})(1+4\text{i}) \\ (1-\text{i})(1+\text{i})+(1+\text{i})(1-\text{i})+2(1+4\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2+4\text{i})+(-\text{i}-1)+17 \\ 2+2+(2+8\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18+3\text{i} \\ 6+8\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

$$

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} & -1+2\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 3+\text{i} \\ -1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-3\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (1-3\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(1-\text{i}) \\ (2+2\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (2+2\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(1-\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10\text{i}+(-1-3\text{i}) & (6-8\text{i})+(1+3\text{i}) \\ (8+4\text{i})+2\text{i} & (4+8\text{i})+(-2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1-13\text{i} & 7-5\text{i} \\ 8+6\text{i} & 4+6\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15

If A=[1−3i−1+2i2+2i1−i] and B=[3−i3+i−1+i1−i], then AB=

a
[−1−13i7−5i8+6i4+6i]
b
[4+6i7−5i8+6i−1−13i]
c
[−1+13i7+5i8+6i4+6i]
d
[−1−13i8+6i7−5i4+6i]
e
[4+6i8+6i7−5i−1−13i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

AB=[1−3i−1+2i2+2i1−i]⋅[3−i3+i−1+i1−i]=[(1−3i)(3−i)+(−1+2i)(−1+i)(1−3i)(3+i)+(−1+2i)(1−i)(2+2i)(3−i)+(1−i)(−1+i)(2+2i)(3+i)+(1−i)(1−i)]=[−10i+(−1−3i)(6−8i)+(1+3i)(8+4i)+2i(4+8i)+(−2i)]=[−1−13i7−5i8+6i4+6i].

content.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} & -1+2\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} & 3+\text{i} \\ -1+\text{i} & 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-3\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (1-3\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(1-\text{i}) \\ (2+2\text{i})(3-\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(-1+\text{i}) & (2+2\text{i})(3+\text{i})+(1-\text{i})(1-\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10\text{i}+(-1-3\text{i}) & (6-8\text{i})+(1+3\text{i}) \\ (8+4\text{i})+2\text{i} & (4+8\text{i})+(-2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1-13\text{i} & 7-5\text{i} \\ 8+6\text{i} & 4+6\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

{R}_{1}=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following  elementary row operations:

$$
{R}_{1}=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Given the matrix A=[2−i2i+13i−2], find the result of applying to A the following elementary row operation: R2:=R2+(−3i2−i)R1

a
[2−i2i+10i]
b
[2−i2i+101]
c
[2−i2i+11i]
d
[2−i3i01]
e
[2−i2i+111]
Submit

decision.explanation: The first entry of R₂ becomes 3i−3i=0. Since 1+2i=i(2−i), the second becomes −2−3i·i=1. R₁ stays unchanged.

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3\text{i}}{2-\text{i}}){R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{+}1 \\ 3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3\text{i}}{2-\text{i}}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 3\text{i}+(-\frac{3\text{i}(2-\text{i})}{2-\text{i}}) & -2+(-\frac{3\text{i}(2\text{i}+1)}{2-\text{i}})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 0 & \frac{(-4+2\text{i})+(6-3\text{i})}{2-\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3\text{i}}{2-\text{i}}){R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{+}1 \\ 3\text{i} & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3\text{i}}{2-\text{i}}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 3\text{i}+(-\frac{3\text{i}(2-\text{i})}{2-\text{i}}) & -2+(-\frac{3\text{i}(2\text{i}+1)}{2-\text{i}})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 0 & \frac{(-4+2\text{i})+(6-3\text{i})}{2-\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} & 2\text{i}+1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 18
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7 & 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{7}{\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7 & 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{7}{\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 7+(-\text{i})\cdot \frac{7}{\text{i}} & \text{(}3-2\text{i})+i\cdot \frac{7}{\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 0 & 10-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 0 & 10-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 18

Given the matrix A=[−ii73−2i], find the result of applying to A the following elementary row operations: R2:=R2+7iR1

a
[ii18i]
b
[−ii110−2i]
c
[−ii08i]
d
[−ii010−2i]
e
[−1108]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let's apply the row operations to A:

A=[−ii73−2i]R2:=R2+7iR1∼[−ii7+(−i)⋅7i(3−2i)+i⋅7i]∼[−ii010−2i]

Therefore, the result is [−ii010−2i].
